note: Bay water levels the explorer offers. All are still water (no waves) in feet NAVD88 unless 'waves' says otherwise. 'category' is the provenance: sourced = stated in the source; derived = arithmetic on sourced values; inference = our reading of an unclear source. Rows cite SOURCE_NOTES.

scenarios.label: Scott Ferris's 12 ft (Oct 22, 2026)
scenarios.source: Scott Ferris, Budget and Finance Policy Committee, 2026-10-22, as quoted by Kelly Hammargren: a "5 or 10-year storm" "could result in a 12-foot sea level rise in the waterfront" (M1). Read here as a 12 ft NAVD88 water level (M2, inference). Unconfirmed: its source, its datum, and whether it includes waves. As still water it is above the 500-year level (10.91, W11); FEMA's wave-inclusive flood elevations on the exposed Marina shoreline are 12 to 14 ft (W6), and a still-water fill shows no waves.

scenarios.label: Bay reaches the flats behind I-80
scenarios.source: Lowest level, to the nearest 0.01 ft above, at which the connected fill reaches the transfer station and the West Berkeley flats over the surface: the highest ground on the water's route is 13.35 ft NAVD88, just east of I-80 about 250 m south of Gilman St (tools/overtop.mjs; SOURCE_NOTES C6). The Draft EIR's ART-based maps put the site's first flooding at MHHW plus 84 inches, about 13.2 ft NAVD88 (F9).
